overview: The Pomodoro timer alternates a focused work interval with a short break. Set the work length and break length, press Start, and the display counts down the current phase. When a phase reaches zero, the timer switches to the next phase and prepares it, but it does not start automatically, so you decide when the next block begins.

The classic Pomodoro Technique uses 25 minutes of focused work followed by a five-minute break, repeating four times before a longer rest. The fixed interval is less important than the habit: a short, defined block lowers the cost of starting, and a scheduled break reduces the temptation to drift into unrelated tasks. You can adjust both lengths to suit deep work, study sessions or chores.

The timer runs entirely in the page. It does not play a sound or send a notification, so keep the tab visible or check back when the block ends. Because browsers throttle timers in background tabs, a heavily backgrounded tab may drift by a few seconds; treat the display as a guide rather than a stopwatch.
useCases: Work through a task in a 25-minute focused block.
Study in repeated intervals with short breaks.
Limit time spent on a single chore or admin task.
Structure a writing session into manageable sprints.
Practise a deliberate work-rest rhythm without installing an app.
pomodoro-timer.workedExample: Set work to 25 minutes and break to 5 minutes, then press Start. The phase indicator shows Work and the display counts down from 25:00. At zero, the status changes to "Work finished. Time for a break", the phase switches to Break and the display resets to 05:00. Press Start again for the break; when it ends, the timer prepares the next 25-minute work block and waits for you.
limits: There is no audible alarm, browser notification or long-break scheduling; the visual display is the only signal.
Timers may drift when the tab is in the background because browsers throttle JavaScript timers to save power.
Changing the work or break length does not alter the current countdown until the next reset or phase change.
Only one timer runs at a time, and no session history or statistics are stored.
pomodoro-timer.privacy: The timer and your interval settings stay in the page. Nothing is uploaded, and no history is saved after you leave.

faq.q: Does it start the break automatically?
faq.a: No. It switches to the break phase and prepares the countdown, but you press Start to begin it. This gives you control over when the break starts.

faq.q: Why did the timer lose a few seconds in the background?
faq.a: Browsers throttle timers in inactive tabs. For precise timing, keep the tab visible or use a dedicated timer app.

faq.q: Can I use a 50-minute work block?
faq.a: Yes. Enter 50 in the work field and press Reset; the next work phase will use that length.

overview: The sleep cycle calculator suggests bedtimes or wake times based on 90-minute sleep cycles plus a 15-minute buffer for falling asleep. In bedtime mode you enter when you plan to go to bed and see wake times for three to six cycles; in wake mode you enter the time you need to get up and see matching bedtimes.

Sleep is not a single uniform state. It moves through cycles of light sleep, deep sleep and REM, each lasting roughly 70 to 120 minutes, with about 90 minutes as a common average. Waking in the middle of deep sleep often feels much worse than waking at the end of a cycle, which is the idea behind cycle-based timing. The 15-minute buffer accounts for the time between lying down and actually falling asleep.

The results are planning suggestions, not medical advice. Individual cycle length varies, sleep debt and stress change how quickly you fall asleep, and the calculator does not know how tired you are. Use it to choose a plausible bedtime, then adjust based on how you actually feel over several nights.
useCases: Choose a bedtime that aligns with a target wake time.
See which wake times follow complete cycles after a given bedtime.
Plan around an early flight or a fixed morning meeting.
Compare four, five and six cycles for a late evening.
Understand why waking mid-cycle can feel groggy.
sleep-cycle-calculator.workedExample: Choose bedtime mode and enter 23:00. With a 15-minute buffer and 90-minute cycles, the suggestions are 03:45 for three cycles, 05:15 for four, 06:45 for five and 08:15 for six. If you need to wake at 07:00, switch to wake mode: the matching bedtimes are 21:45 the previous evening for six cycles, 23:15 for five, 00:45 for four and 02:15 for three.
limits: Every person's cycle length differs, and it can vary from night to night; a fixed 90-minute assumption is only an average.
The 15-minute fall-asleep buffer is a fixed estimate and does not account for insomnia, caffeine, stress or sleep debt.
Times are calculated for the local device clock and do not adjust for daylight saving changes or travel across time zones.
It is a planning aid, not a diagnosis or treatment for a sleep disorder; persistent problems need professional advice.
sleep-cycle-calculator.privacy: Bedtime and wake times are calculated locally in your browser and are never uploaded or stored.

faq.a: It approximates the time it takes to fall asleep. If you usually take longer or shorter, mentally adjust the suggested times.

faq.q: How many cycles should I aim for?
faq.a: Most adults need seven to nine hours, which is roughly five or six cycles. The calculator shows three to six so you can choose based on your schedule.

faq.q: Can this fix my sleep schedule?
faq.a: It can help you choose consistent times, but it is not a treatment. Persistent insomnia or daytime sleepiness should be assessed by a clinician.
